summary: The paper offers a coherent theoretical story for the 'PCC plateau' observed when jointly training attention regressors with MSE+PCC losses, identifying (i) a 1/σ_y attenuation of the PCC gradient and (ii) a convex-hull capacity ceiling on any convex aggregator, then proposes ECA with three targeted modules (SRA, DATS, DNPL). Empirical gains are consistent across synthetic, tabular, spatial-transcriptomics, and MSA benchmarks. However, the analysis leans on well-known properties of PCC (scale invariance) with restrictive conditions, several experimental gains fall within the reported inter-fold variance, and stat significance, baselines, and reproducibility detail are all thin for an ICLR paper.
strengths: The theory-to-method mapping is unusually clean: each of SRA, DATS, and DNPL is motivated by a specific identified bottleneck (convex-hull radius, homogeneity-driven attention flattening, 1/σ_y gradient attenuation).

Proposition 2.1's MSE mean–std–correlation decomposition, together with Lemma 2.1's scale invariance, gives an intuitive explanation for the empirical plateau that is easy for practitioners to internalize.
The convex-hull PCC gain bound (Theorem 2.2) is a novel and useful angle on softmax-attention capacity in the regression setting.

Experiments span four qualitatively different regimes (controllable-homogeneity synthetic, UCI tabular, pathology spatial-transcriptomics, multimodal sentiment), and ablations remove SRA/DATS/DNPL individually.
The synthetic-data sweep over σ ∈ {0.10, 0.24, 0.42, 0.73} directly stress-tests the predicted dependence on in-sample homogeneity.

key_concerns.issue: Statistical significance is not established for the headline gains. On 10xProteomic (Table 3) the standard deviations for PCC@F/S/M are 0.16–0.20, larger than or comparable to the reported ~0.09 improvements over EGN; only three folds are shown and no paired test, seed variance, or confidence interval is reported. UCI and synthetic tables likewise lack seeds/error bars, so ~1–4 point PCC gains cannot be distinguished from run-to-run noise.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report ≥5 seeds with mean±std per cell for every table, run paired significance tests (e.g., Wilcoxon or paired t) on per-fold/per-seed results, and add error bars to Figures 5/6/8/9. Given the fold-level variance on 10xProteomic, additional folds or bootstrap CIs are needed.

key_concerns.issue: The scope of Theorem 2.2 is narrower than the prose suggests. It requires R < σ_0/‖w‖_2 and only bounds |ρ − ρ_0| relative to mean-pooling; when R ≥ σ_0/‖w‖_2 the bound is vacuous. The paper describes this as a 'fundamental capacity limit' of any convex aggregator, but the result is really a local sensitivity bound near mean pooling. This should be scoped more carefully — mean-pooling is not the optimal convex aggregator, so 'ceiling' language overreaches.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Reframe the claim as a Lipschitz-style bound of PCC around mean-pooling, discuss when the condition R < σ_0/‖w‖_2 holds on real data, and provide either a matching lower/upper bound against the optimal convex aggregator or an empirical characterization of tightness.

key_concerns.issue: Novelty of the optimization-dynamics analysis is oversold. The 1/σ_y attenuation follows almost immediately from the standard fact that PCC is scale-invariant while MSE is not, and Corollary 2.1's O(1/σ_y^{3/2}) rate assumes ρ ∈ [0,1] (i.e., excludes early training where ρ ≤ 0 is common) and uses one particular RMS ratio. The stated bound does not clearly prove attenuation dominates in practice — it only bounds a ratio.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Position the gradient decomposition as a re-derivation for the attention setting rather than a novel bottleneck discovery; discuss the ρ ∈ [0,1] regime restriction; and show empirically that the derived rate matches observed gradient ratios across datasets, not only in the synthetic case (Figure 3).

key_concerns.issue: Baselines against correlation-oriented alternatives are missing. There is no comparison to obvious alternatives that also target correlation: CCC loss, differentiable Spearman/rank losses (e.g., soft-rank, Blondel et al.), listwise ranking losses, distribution-matching losses (moment-matching, Sinkhorn), or non-convex attention pooling variants (gated attention pooling, set transformers, PMA). Without these, it is not clear whether ECA's gains come from the specific mechanisms proposed or from any correlation-aware objective/non-convex aggregator.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add at least (i) a differentiable rank-loss baseline, (ii) a non-convex pooling baseline such as gated attention or PMA, and (iii) a temperature-only or residual-only attention variant to isolate whether the gains truly require the ECA-specific parameterization of γ_s and τ_s.

key_concerns.issue: DNPL is presented as principled but is essentially a StopGrad rescaling by σ_y that exactly cancels the 1/σ_y factor. This risks amplifying noise when σ_y is small early in training and changing effective PCC weighting from the user-specified λ_PCC. There is no analysis of stability, no comparison to simply increasing λ_PCC, and no ablation of the StopGrad choice.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add ablations: (a) DNPL with vs. without StopGrad, (b) DNPL vs. tuned λ_PCC schedule (linear/curriculum) matched in effective magnitude, (c) sensitivity to initial σ_y. Discuss failure modes when σ_y ≈ 0.

key_concerns.issue: Reproducibility detail is thin. Hyperparameters β, T_min, γ_max, λ_γ, MLP architecture for γ_s, optimizer, learning rate, batch size, warmup, and stopping criteria are not stated in the body. Anonymization does not excuse missing procedural detail.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a concise methods box listing all hyperparameters used per dataset, the γ_s MLP architecture, and training schedule; include ranges and selection procedure.

key_concerns.issue: The claim that the analysis is 'backbone-agnostic' because most attention regressors end in a convex pooling head is strong. Deep transformer stacks earlier can also produce shape information, and the analysis in Section 2.3 assumes a specific single-layer aggregation. Section E is referenced but only in the appendix.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Move the multi-layer/backbone applicability argument into the main text with a clearer statement of what is and is not covered, and, ideally, an experiment where ECA is inserted at multiple attention layers rather than only the final aggregator.

key_concerns.issue: Related work is thin: correlation-oriented ranking/CCC losses, work on softmax expressivity (Bhojanapalli et al., Yang et al.) is cited but not engaged with, and set-encoder / non-convex pooling literature (DeepSets, Set Transformer PMA, gated attention pooling, ABMIL) is not discussed even though SRA is closely related.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a paragraph explicitly contrasting SRA with gated attention pooling / PMA / ABMIL, and DNPL with CCC and rank-based losses.

questions_for_authors: Are the reported gains on 10xProteomic statistically significant given the per-fold standard deviations exceed the mean gaps? Can you provide paired tests over seeds and folds?
In Corollary 2.1 you assume ρ ∈ [0,1]. Early training routinely has ρ < 0; does the attenuation story still hold quantitatively there, and does Figure 3 include that regime?
How tight is the condition R < σ_0/‖w‖_2 in Theorem 2.2 across your real datasets? Please report the actual R and σ_0/‖w‖_2 per dataset.

How does ECA compare to (a) a differentiable rank / CCC loss with a standard softmax attention, and (b) a gated-attention or PMA pooling with the same MSE+PCC objective? These are natural ablations for the 'extrapolate beyond hull' and 'correlation-aware objective' axes.

In DATS, τ_s is monotonically increasing in in-sample dispersion, so more heterogeneous samples get higher temperature (softer attention). This is the opposite direction that Remark 2.3 motivates; please clarify or fix the sign.
For DNPL, does the StopGrad break the fixed points of the joint objective in practice? What happens if σ_y collapses at initialization?
How sensitive are results to γ_max, λ_γ, T_min, and β? A sensitivity table would clarify whether ECA's gains rely on careful tuning per dataset.
Why is only one MSA baseline (ALMT) augmented with ECA? Does ECA also improve MISA, MulT, or DLF, or is the gain specific to the ALMT architecture?
calibration_check: Claims are directionally supported but overreach in two places: Theorem 2.2 is described as a fundamental capacity ceiling when it is a local bound near mean-pooling under a restrictive condition, and the 10xProteomic 'significant improvement' language is not matched by an appropriate significance test given the large inter-fold variance.

significance.justification: The PCC plateau is a real, practically annoying phenomenon in shape-sensitive regression, and a principled fix would be useful to a substantial subcommunity (pathology, MSA, tabular).

novelty.justification: The convex-hull PCC bound is a genuinely novel angle; the 1/σ_y gradient analysis is a solid re-derivation but follows fairly directly from well-known PCC scale invariance and softmax Jacobians.

rigor.justification: Derivations are internally consistent, but Corollary 2.1 restricts to ρ ∈ [0,1] and Theorem 2.2 requires R < σ_0/‖w‖_2 and only bounds against mean-pooling, weaker than the 'capacity limit of any convex aggregator' framing suggests.

statistical_soundness.justification: No seed variance for UCI/synthetic/MSA; 10xProteomic reports large stds that swamp the reported gains; no paired significance tests anywhere; sample sizes per fold are small.

calibration_honesty.justification: Most claims are scoped, but 'fundamental capacity limit,' 'breaking the PCC plateau,' and 'significant improvements' are stronger than the reported evidence given variance and restrictive theorem conditions.

clarity.justification: The narrative arc is clear, but notation is heavy (as, bs, y, ȳ, σ_y, σ_s, R_s, γ_s, τ_s) and the presentation of DATS's temperature direction (higher τ for more dispersion) reads inconsistently with its stated motivation.

structure_compliance.justification: Standard ICLR structure with theory, method, and experiments; appendix pointers are appropriate; length feels reasonable for the content.

reproducibility.justification: Method equations are precise, but hyperparameters (β, T_min, γ_max, λ_γ), γ_s MLP architecture, optimizer/LR, and training budget per dataset are not detailed in the body; anonymization does not explain these omissions.

related_work.justification: Correlation-loss and softmax-expressivity threads are cited superficially; missing engagement with ranking/CCC losses and non-convex pooling (PMA, gated attention, ABMIL) which are the most natural comparators for both DNPL and SRA.

figure_quality.justification: Captions describe informative comparisons (gradient ratio decay, per-fold training curves, homogeneity sweep) that directly support the theoretical claims, though several rely on visual trends that would benefit from CI bands.

breadth_generality.justification: Four settings across synthetic/tabular/pathology/multimodal is a real strength, but each is tested with essentially one backbone and lacks the multi-model breadth needed to justify the 'drop-in replacement' generality claim.

overall_recommendation.justification: Borderline reject: coherent story with real gains but under-tested significance, restrictive theory framed as fundamental, and missing correlation-loss / non-convex-pooling baselines that are directly comparable.
